title: Hebrews Bible Quiz - Chapter 2
description: Ten questions on Hebrews 2: the warning not to drift away, the words about man crowned with glory, and the one who shared in flesh and blood to help his brothers.

questions.text: Why should we pay greater attention to the things that were heard?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 says we ought to pay greater attention to the things that were heard, lest perhaps we drift away.

answers.text: So that we may teach others
So that we do not drift away
So that the angels may hear
So that we may be made rich

questions.text: The salvation first spoken through the Lord was confirmed to us by whom?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 says this great salvation was at the first spoken through the Lord, and was confirmed to us by those who heard.

questions.text: How did God testify along with them, according to verse 4?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 says God testified with them by signs and wonders, by various works of power, and by gifts of the Holy Spirit, according to his own will.

questions.text: To whom did he not subject the world to come?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says he did not subject the world to come, of which the text speaks, to angels.

questions.text: With what is the one made a little lower than the angels crowned?
questions.explanation: Verse 7 says, "You made him a little lower than the angels. You crowned him with glory and honor."

questions.text: Who is named in verse 9 as the one we see crowned, because of the suffering of death?
questions.explanation: Verse 9 says we see him who has been made a little lower than the angels, Jesus, crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death.

questions.text: What is he not ashamed to call those who are sanctified?
questions.explanation: Verse 11 says that both he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all from one, and for that reason he is not ashamed to call them brothers.

questions.text: Who is named in verse 14 as the one who had the power of death?
questions.explanation: Verse 14 says that through death he might bring to nothing him who had the power of death, that is, the devil.

questions.text: To whom does verse 16 say he gives help, rather than to angels?
questions.explanation: Verse 16 says that most certainly he does not give help to angels, but he gives help to the offspring of Abraham.

answers.text: To the children of the fathers
To the house of the servants
To the rulers of the nations

questions.text: Because he himself suffered being tempted, whom is he able to help?
questions.explanation: Verse 18 says that because he himself has suffered being tempted, he is able to help those who are tempted.
